items: One counter per distinct URL lives in RAM: the working set is cardinality times per-entry overhead
Hot partitions aggregate in memory while cold ones spill; both are correct, only the cost differs
OOM is a wrong-answer failure, not slowness: the job dies instead of finishing late
cards.title: Bounded Memory

items: Spilling a partition to disk is the escape hatch when the working set passes RAM
Hash spill keeps exact counts: slower from I/O, never approximate
The spill threshold is environment-specific: measure it, never quote a universal URL count
cards.title: Spill Is the Escape Hatch

items: Hash aggregation wins while distinct keys fit comfortably in RAM
Skewed logs aggregate fast: a few hot URLs dominate the counts
Past the spill point, the sort path usually wins on total time
cards.title: When Hash Wins

meta.title: Hash Aggregation Under a Memory Cap
